finding: Machine-readable pricing contradicted the available PayPal checkout.
evidence: The production Pricing page exposed PayPal Offers while pricing.txt and llms.txt said checkout was unavailable and retained a 2026-08-12 status date.
impact: Search engines and AI agents could receive a false purchase state and provide users with stale commercial answers.
fix: Align pricing.txt and llms.txt with PayPal Business recurring subscriptions, package prices, refunds, checkout availability, and the public-tool allowance boundary; protect the wording with tests.

finding: The LUFS guide stated that paid batch checkout remained unavailable.
evidence: The article body contradicted the live Basic and Pro PayPal subscription checkout.
impact: A high-intent article could discourage valid purchases and repeat stale payment information in search and AI results.
fix: Update the article body, summary state, and last-modified date while preserving the separate public-downloader allowance boundary.

finding: Pricing and Audio Toolkit inherited homepage social metadata.
evidence: Pricing lacked an independent Twitter card and Audio Toolkit lacked independent Open Graph and Twitter definitions and product images.
impact: Commercial URLs could render generic previews with weaker relevance and click-through intent.
fix: Give each commercial page a canonical URL, distinct Open Graph and Twitter metadata, and a dedicated 1200 by 630 image route.

finding: Inner pages inherited homepage or collection structured data and duplicate entities.
evidence: The locale layout emitted a homepage WebPage and breadcrumb on every route, and the tools layout emitted CollectionPage schema on tool detail pages.
impact: Conflicting canonical entities make page meaning and rich-result eligibility less clear.
fix: Limit global schema to Organization and WebSite, then let each page own its WebPage subtype, breadcrumb, and product or application entity.

finding: English-only commercial routes advertised redirecting localized hreflang targets.
evidence: next-intl generated alternate links such as localized Pricing routes even though non-English entries redirect to English.
impact: Search engines receive alternates that are not equivalent localized documents.
fix: Disable framework-generated alternate Link headers and keep page-owned English and x-default alternates for English-only commercial pages.
source: Production response and repository routing audit, 2026-08-23

finding: Blog, About, and VIN metadata did not match their search intent.
evidence: Blog reused homepage metadata, About had the title About and inherited the homepage graph, and VIN metadata exceeded typical snippet ranges.
impact: Generic or truncated snippets weaken relevance, trust, and click-through rate.
fix: Add page-specific titles, descriptions, canonical and social metadata, ProfilePage or CollectionPage schema, and concise VIN copy.

finding: BlogPosting author URLs resolved to avatar images instead of an author profile.
evidence: BlogPosting constructed author.url from the avatar path.
impact: Articles could not resolve their author to a stable Person or ProfilePage entity.
fix: Link BlogPosting, About ProfilePage, Person, and Organization with stable IDs and use /about/ as the author URL.

finding: The tools ItemList exposed repeated low-information descriptions.
evidence: Six catalog entries repeated the same short phrase three times in data consumed by the tools CollectionPage.
impact: Templated text weakens entity precision for search and AI systems.
fix: Replace each placeholder with a distinct task, input, output, and constraint description.

finding: Current site-wide indexing and performance outcomes remain unverified.
evidence: This implementation has no current GSC export, complete 661-URL crawl, server logs, or current 28-day CrUX sample. The older 259 ms INP measurement is not current evidence.
impact: A current SEO score or claim of production success would be unsupported.
fix: After deployment, crawl the sitemap and inspect GSC, logs, headers, rendered metadata, and 28-day CrUX before reprioritizing performance or content work.
